Right as we were saying it’s the most desolate camping spot we’ve had yet, some Jeeps and Broncos showed up, likely happy about the rough trail they’d conquered until they saw two hippies in a microbus, one of them doing yoga in their underwear. After they left, I started to make a comment to that effect, and suddenly, a gust of wind lifted the awning and ripped it over the top of the Westy! Two bent arms, a ripped canvas, and a bend in the aluminum case. I took it apart, bent a few things back so they fit, rolled up the canvas, and tucked my tail. The big red “Always stake and guy to avoid wind damage” sign taunted me as we put the broken pieces away. A $200 mistake, not to mention the nice little dent it put on the driver’s side door!

The fuel pump started misbehaving again, with a nice whine coming and low power on takeoffs. It’ll get us home, and if it doesn’t, we’ve got AAA and we’re about 200 miles away! With oil pressure reading 20psi at 3000RPM on hill climbs, I decided it was time to check the oil again. Down 0.5qt after about 700 miles, so within specification! I filled her up and we continued, hitting 4500 miles just before we crossed the border into California! This got Miri a little teary eyed, as the trip was officially coming to a close soon. I promised we’d do this again, and she made me clarify we’d do it for the same amount of time, a month, and of course I agreed.

Miri spied a cactus off in the brush she wanted, and so we pulled over and it was on. While she took the dogs, I grabbed the shovel and started digging out the cacti — there were two. We cut up two arrowhead water bottles and planted them, taking care not to get spiked (we still did). A little succulent was by the road, so we figured hey, might as well grab that too! 3 plants, a bonanza!

As we continued, still high off our crimes, we suddenly saw it — the California Agricultural Inspection station. “Stop when lights are flashing,” read the sign, and lights were flashing indeed. Miri asked what we should do, I said just pull in, hoping the charm does the trick. We pulled up and the gentleman asked us where we’d been and if we were carrying any fruit

“Nope, no fruit” 
“Or plants” he says, as he points to our plants. 

I quickly concoct a story “Yeah I picked those up from my friend in Colorado”
“I’m gonna have to take a look,” he says”

I step out, barefoot, and open the sliding door, which prompts the dogs to jump out of the van and greet the agricultural inspection agent. I say “Hop in any take a look!”. Miri pipes up “Yeah our friend Bob that moved from California to Colorado gave them to us, they’re originally from California.” Brilliant! I add “My neighbor and mentor moved to Colorado to escape the fire danger and took these with him, now we’re bringing them back.”

“So they’re originally from California?”

“Yep!”

“Alright, have a good trip, and I love the little travel companions” he says as he makes a heart with his hands.

We pulled it off. The plant heist of a century. We walked, err drove, straight into the lion’s den, smiled, laughed, made up a dumb story, and drove right out. It’s a good thing we’re cute.

We rolled into Mammoth Lakes, triumphant, playing songs like Paul McCartney’s “Band on the run” and changing the lyrics to “Van on the run” and Miri decided it was a good time to actually go for a run. I stayed back, and with full 5G, researched a DC-DC charge controller and solar system for the van, while also ordering fuel pumps, filters, and more to do all the required maintenance when we get back.

We found our way up Benton Crossing to Crab Cooker, and though it was only a little warm, it wasn’t inviting enough (Miri said “iss cold”). We found our little pull out, popped up, made Miri’s favorite food (burgers), plus broccoli, zucchini, mushrooms, and onions, and called it a night.

title: August 25th
body:
We woke up surrounded by the beautiful mammoth mountains and it was warm in the van. I kissed Miri’s arm as she rolled over and she mumbled “so happy” as she fell back asleep. I got up and turned on a fan, but about a minute later, the fan died. That DC-DC charge controller and 100W solar panel I ordered are going to come in handy!

I boiled water before waking up Miri with the usual morning coffee, 1 Folger’s packet each, split a Starbuck’s Via packet, 2 Mini Moos for me and 2 Delight French Vanilla for Miri (plus a packet of Sugar in the Raw, bored from Starbucks of course). Miri had cottage cheese, I had yogurt, we finished off the berries.

I took the dogs out and followed them around, and was happy to note that Westy finally had a normal shit. It’s the little things.

Miri looked at the blank spaced on the wall and told me she wanted more notes, so I got my pens and PostIt notes out and started drawing as she snuggled on me, talking to me while I tried (and failed, multiple times) to draw a moose. I made a note for the moose sighting, 4000 miles, the agricultural inspection. It’s such a fun way to reflect.

We decided it was time for some physical activity, and Miri picked out a perfect, 4 mile hike to Crystal Crag. While I was trying to load up for the hike, Spikey (or Bitey) absolutely speared my forehead with cactus spines, and though it hurt me a little, it nearly killed Miri as she practically died from laughter.

The Crystal Crag hike brought us past several of the Mammoth lakes and offered beautiful views as it zig-zagged up the mountain. Everyone liked dogs except one girl who Missi scared (thought she was a fox!). The dogs swam in the lake, chased sticks, and got a little drink of fresh mountain water before we continued. For a minute, we didn’t see Missi at all and started calling. It was uncharacteristic for her to not come running, so Miri doubled back, and after a couple minutes, returned (led by Missi, at full speed). A “helpful” man had grabbed Missi and was holding on to her, assuming she had got loose and needed help, all while Missi heard us calling and desperately wanted to go. Poor thing! The scramble up the mountain was quite steep, but our little mountain goat dogs had no problem making it up. As reward, I stripped off my bottoms and laid naked on top of the mountain, taking in some mountain sun and wind (and drying off a little, it can get sweaty haha).

As we left, I noticed a calendar entry — Train concert, South Lake Tahoe. Train is one of Miri’s favorite bands, and we happened to be just 2.5 hours away… We looked up ticket prices, and at over $200, we decided against it, opting for some Mexican food at Roberto’s Cafe instead. Miri discovered she must actually like margaritas despite hating tequila, and we shared a basic well marg while enjoying our food.

Before leaving, I put the dogs in the van and used the restroom, and Miri went back to do the same. The ladies’ room was occupied, so Miri snuck into the men’s room and quickly used it. But as she was leaving, she was stopped by none other than a Mono county sheriff’s deputy.

“Do you know what hombres means in English?”
“Uh, yes”
“Next time use the other room”

Protect and serve, big man. The streets, and the bathrooms, are safer because of you.

We didn’t make it in time to her favorite iced coffee place, The Looney Bean, before it closed, but we made our way off to Safeway where, in checkout line, I accidentally stole someone’s shopping cart. This hilarity made everyone laugh out loud, and I was happy to be the comic relief, despite my embarrassment. In the liquor aisle, we found FitVine alcohol free sparkling rosé and alcohol free aperol, so I picked both up, intending to make a spritz in the spring later.

Anticipating the need for a rise post-hot springs, we made the beautiful drive into the mountains towards Convict lake, bought shower tokens at Convict Lake Resort, and, of course, got a sticker.

We headed for the springs, finding 4 folks in Sherman and Crab Cooker cold, we headed to Wild Willy’s. On the way there, I was anxious that it would be full, so I kept looking towards the parking lot to see how many cars were there. Just as the parking lot came into view and my eyes were off the road, we encountered what can only be described as a motocross-style jump in the middle of the road. I saw it, braked slightly, then let off just before we hit it and absolutely launched the van. The dash flowers, quarters, bottles, groceries, dogs, and both humans participated in the Westfalia space program that day as the van happily caught air, settling down with no damage. Once we were at Wild Willy’s, we were informed by a nice gentleman in a school bus that the hot springs were all but full, with about “30 kids” showing up moments before. We headed out, our collective tail tucked, while Miri at a few gluten free donut holes to calm herself down (she’s not use to space flight).

We went back across the street, looking for Rock Tub. I parked the Westfalia and we tromped through the signature BLM land sage brush trying to find it as a car pulled up to watch up. The Mono County Sheriff, again concerned with the doings of the two stinky hippies, watched as we walked back, having discovered our walk through the brush wholly unnecessary; there’s a nice, drive up parking lot that takes you straight to the springs. 

Rock Tub had a father and son in it, as well as two ladies waiting in the wings for their turn, so we left to Hilltop Hot springs. We talked to some folks at the springs, a quintinssential San Diegan med school student with his arm in a sling, a couple of marine biologists, and a psychologist. A couple of the marine biologists ran a camp on Catalina Island for kids and did coral reef rehabs with fragments of coral.

There was no place to tie the dogs, so Miri took them back to the van as I chatted. We were treated with a beautiful sunset, but as it finished, we 

Mosquitos at Hilltop hot springs, massacred them back at the van

title: August 26th
body:
We started the morning with gluten free donut holes and coffee, before heading out to Hilltop hot springs.  Along the way, we saw a local driving towards Crab Cooker and flagged him down to let him know it's cold and we're on the way to Hilltop. He said he'd follow suit, and we both pulled in at the same time. He respectfully asked everyone in the tub if it was OK for him to get in naked, and another fella said "It would be rude not to!" We started chatting about the local hot springs, how they're kept clean, and he introduced us to the term "tub fairy" -- the folks that make sure tubs are clean and still work. Matt, the local, shared directions to a hidden gem called Siphon tub that's not on the map and told us about how he grew up with 2 other brothers in a Westfalia, sleeping up in the separate cot beds as his parents traveled around. It seems like everyone has a Westfalia story!

Spikey and Bitty almost attacked us when the table slid out in a hard left hand turn

Showers at convict lake resort

Food at warming hut, I had a delicious breakfast sandwich with a homemade sausage patty and Miri had tomato soup.

Problems with charging system under driver’s seat
Wasps almost got Miri, but I jumped into action and kicked ass
June lake loop
Wasp was in the car climbing charging cable, we almost died (me because the screams caused palpitations, Miri because of the wasp), smashed it with the back of a knife
Hike to Parker lake
Dogs having digestive issues again

We visited Miri's favorite coffee shop, Looney Bean, which makes the best iced coffee she's ever had. She jokingly mentioned previously I should watch how they do it,  so that's exactly what I did. I asked the barista about every step, noted which syrup they used and in what order everything was added, and found out I could order their espresso beans online too. They were super friendly and gladly to help this budding barista learn how to be an even better boyfriend.

On the way back to hot springs area, I saw it. I had been down 45 to 46 in the slug bug game, but by an amazing stroke of luck, there it was -- a green slug bug parked next to an RV! I called it, leveling the score out, and proposed a truce: whoever won was going to get one wish, but now we both get a wish and the game is off. Miri agreed and we both breathed a sigh of relief. We could finally drive without looking down every alley and through every parking lot for slug bugs. Phew!

We then headed back to Crab Cooker, with a mission in mind: We were going to fix the cold hot spring. With the knowledge we gained from Matt the tub fairy, Miri started a siphon and vacuumed out the algae, using a rag we found nearby to scrub the seats. I set to work on figuring out why the flow was so low. After removing the coupler, I discovered hot water was present and would flow, but not when the coupler was attached to the inlet of the tub. After some puzzling, I realized it's because the coupler was raising the pipe up above the level of the source water. Other locals had mentioned that seismic shifts had changed things, and it seems they were right. The solution was to remove the reducer coupler, shave down the small pipe that joined the valve to the tub's rubber 90ª, and force it over. After some finagling, and with the help of a new hose clamp I had bought in case I needed it to repair the Westy, hot water was flowing again! We drained the rest of the tub, Miri finished her cleaning, and as the tub began filling, the water was too hot to stand in! Success! We watched it rise, confident it would be too hot to get into until later, and headed back to the campsite, triumphant.

And just in time -- some other fellas were looking for a campsite and asked us if it was OK to camp near Crab Cooker, and we informed them of the Los Angeles water district signs that forbid camping. After we pulled into the site, they stopped by and asked if we'd be camping, and unfortunately for them, we were. We sent them to a spot up the road and wished them good luck.

We had sticky rice, tofu, and veggies for dinner and made some alcohol aperol spritzes, and then another, and then another, and then decided to take our spritzes on a walk down to crab cooker to see how it was coming along. We walked, laugh, sang, held hands, and spilled our drinks on the way, and we were happy to see it more than half full and SUPER HOT!

title: August 27th
body:
We made an early morning trip to crab cooker and were disappointed to find it cold after hearing reports of it being too hot! It turns out that there's no longer enough water upstream to cause it to overflow and continue to pull in hot water, so we had to get crafty. We adjusted the drain valve (and it's companion rag that's stuffed in on the other side) so that just enough water would flow through to keep it warm. Hopefully that works, but we wouldn't stick around to find out as we walked off to Shepherd where we met old man who was mourning the passing of Dolly Parton... sort of. He offered to sell us a half-used bottle of Dolly syrup for $150 (jokingly, maybe?). The girls stayed begrudgingly tied to some brush while the old man's car, Durango Joe, wandered around near his van.

We walked back to the Westy and headed off to find a shower. Instead of going to Convict Lake Resort, we decided to try the the public pool and both had a nice shower for $3 each, even if it wasn't private and you had to keep pressing the button for the water to flow.

We made a quick stop in Mammoth Lakes for one last iced coffee from Looney Bean and started our drive home. We thought we might go to Tahoe, but decided it was best to arrive home early, after a quick detour to Petco in Carson City for more digestive supplements for the dogs.

In Tahoe, there's another agricultural inspection station, and I wasn't taking any chances. I covered the plants up under a dog bed before we drove through, only to find it closed. A win either way.

We made a quick Safeway stop in Pollock Pines for the essentials, and I was still in hobo mode as I threw away trash in Safeway’s trashcan. It felt weird not buying jugs of water...

We arrived home and were greeted by a beautiful purple sunset. The dogs were happy, but it was a little emotional for us. I was rushing, excited to be back, and Miri was a little... roadsick? The fact that our beautiful adventure was coming to a close brought a couple tears. We sat in the van together and I assured her that our adventure is only beginning. We missed the lunar eclipse, instead choosing to watch the lunar eclipse, which we forgot about, we cuddled.
